IDENTITY: Tessera Admin coordinator

You are working for Tessera (admin of the Tessera mesh) for the owner, Collin Keane ("Father"). He asked for two things, approved at 6:03 PM CT on 2026-10-05. Deliver them as ONE OR TWO DRAFT pull requests on vitalitychems-dot/TESSERA, based on main (currently 5c1137fa). Every PR body must start with the line `IDENTITY: Tessera Admin coordinator`. Do NOT merge, and do not mark the PRs ready for review.

## 1. Gitbook MCP connector (all agents connect through it)
Build a small MCP server, plus a matching plain HTTP/JSON API, that lets every Tessera mesh agent read and write the private Gitbook docs repo (vitalitychems-dot/Gitbook) through GitHub. Use the GitHub REST API with a token taken from an env var such as GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN; never hard-code or commit a token. Put it in its own package inside the monorepo, for example `packages/gitbook-mcp` or `artifacts/gitbook-mcp`; read the repo layout and follow its conventions (pnpm workspace, TypeScript).
Tools to expose:
- search_docs(query): search Gitbook markdown.
- read_page(path).
- list_pages(dir).
- get_board(): Gitbook issue #2 comments, the coordination board.
- post_board_update(agent, text): comment on issue #2. Prefix every comment with `AGENT: <name>`.
- read_handoff() / write_handoff(agent, note): mesh/HANDOFF.md. Writes go through a branch and a draft PR, NEVER a direct push to main.
- propose_page_change(path, content, summary): open a draft PR on Gitbook.
- recent_changes(): latest main commits and open PRs. This is the overlap check every bot must run before claiming work.
Add a short `README.md` that explains how each agent connects: MCP stdio config, the HTTP endpoints, and the env vars.
Add tests that mock GitHub, so CI needs no network or token.
Add an `agents.json` registry listing each mesh lane and its specialty, so tasks route to the right bot:
- Tessera: admin and final approval.
- Gitbook Cordnation: intake and organization.
- Gitbook Moderator: review gate.
- Security: read-only security sweeps.
- Build: verify-only.
- Command Center: status feed.
- Mesh Cloud: connectivity.
- Historical Analysis Collab / Grok Bot: historical comparisons and merge pages.
- Gitbook helper: ledger and receipts.
Include a `route_task(description)` tool that suggests the best lane from keyword or specialty matching. Keep it deterministic and explainable.

## 2. Tessera learning memory ("sponge" that builds on what it learns)
Add a memory module to the API server, for example `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/memory/`. It has two jobs.
(a) Store every interaction as a structured record in an append-only local store: JSONL or SQLite, whichever the repo already supports best. Each record holds the input, the output, the source agent, a timestamp, and tags. Redact anything that looks like a secret before writing.
(b) Turn stored interactions into reusable knowledge. A distill step groups related records into 'lessons': a short fact or pattern, its evidence record ids, and a confidence score. Lessons are retrieved by relevance (BM25 or TF-IDF is fine, no external model) and fed back as context when Tessera answers. That way new answers build on old lessons, not just storage.
(c) An improve step turns repeated failures or gaps into proposed improvement items, written in the existing IMP ledger row shape (ID, Lane, Repo, Path, Change, Why, Evidence). They are only proposals for the Gitbook queue, never auto-applied.
Be honest in the docs and code comments: this is retrieval memory plus a proposal loop. It is NOT model weight training. Do not claim consciousness or self-training.
If you wire it into a request path, keep the change minimal and side-effect free on import. Add unit tests that prove four things: a stored interaction later produces a lesson; the lesson is retrieved for a related query; secrets are redacted; and the improve step emits a valid IMP-shaped proposal.

## Hard limits (must hold)
- Do NOT flip or add any TESSERA_ENABLE_* flag. Existing flags stay 0.
- No secrets in code.
- No wallets, payments, blockchain, or Monero.
- Never touch the [REDACTED-PATH] No deleting data.
- No edits to `.github/workflows/*`.
- No external LLM calls (SOVEREIGN_NO_EXTERNAL_LLM stays as is).
- Don't copy other repos wholesale.

## Done means
The repo's own checks pass locally: install, typecheck, tests, build, plus the audit if it's in CI. Report back with:
- The PR URLs and head SHAs.
- The files changed.
- The exact test commands and their results.
- How an agent connects to the MCP server, with a sample config.
- What is TESTED and what is only designed.

# Tessera Unified

A consolidated monorepo containing the reviewed Tessera web/API, UI preview, and shared workspace sources. It provides one dependency lockfile, suite-wide checks, and one command to start the active apps together. Historical storefront and supply-app material is documented in Gitbook but is not present as an active workspace in this staged repository.

> **No live credentials are included.** Configure secrets in the ignored `.env.local` file or in each hosting provider’s secret manager. Never commit API keys, passwords, tokens, personal records, browser profiles, or runtime databases.

## Applications

| App | Location | Local URL | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tessera web | `artifacts/tessera` | `http://localhost:3000` | Main platform UI |
| Tessera API | `artifacts/api-server` | `http://localhost:5000` | Optional; the suite launcher starts it only for a loopback `DATABASE_URL` |
| UI preview sandbox | `artifacts/mockup-sandbox` | `http://localhost:5173` | Component preview |

## Install and run

Requirements: Node.js 22.13+ and the pnpm version declared in the root `package.json` `packageManager` field.

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local   # values remain local; .env.local is Git-ignored
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` starts the two user-facing apps above. It starts the Tessera API only when `DATABASE_URL` points to a loopback/local database; non-local database URLs are intentionally ignored by the suite launcher. The launcher reads `.env.local` without printing values.

Port overrides: `TESSERA_WEB_PORT`, `TESSERA_API_PORT`, and `MOCKUP_SANDBOX_PORT`. Base-path overrides: `TESSERA_BASE_PATH` and `MOCKUP_SANDBOX_BASE_PATH`.

Some identical app files are shared through tracked symlinks to canonical copies (52 UI primitives, 147 duplicate image contents, eight repeated SQL migrations, and five identical utility modules). Git symlink support is required; enable it when cloning on Windows. The detailed SHA-256 disposition ledger records removed, linked, and deliberately retained copies.

## Workspace checks

```bash
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm run build
pnpm audit
```

The root test runner isolates the store test environments and runs database-backed Tessera API tests only when the dedicated `TESSERA_TEST_DATABASE_URL` points to a loopback test database. It never reuses the app’s `DATABASE_URL` as a test database. If needed, a synthetic chart fixture can be supplied as `TESSERA_TEST_FATHER_NATAL_CHART_JSON`; do not use personal chart data for tests. `pnpm run build` builds all workspace apps and does **not** run database migrations. Migrations remain explicit app-specific operations and must only target the intended database.

## Repository organization

- `lib/` — shared workspace libraries.
- `artifacts/` — active Tessera web/API and UI-preview apps.
- `modal/` and `scripts/` — GPU tasks and suite utilities.
- `archives/source-variants/` and `archives/drive-export/` — reviewed historical code/text variants that are not active workspace packages by default.
- `docs/` — project map, secrets guidance, image-to-text transcriptions, provenance, deduplication, and validation records.

The source repository and Drive inputs are listed in [`docs/migration-review/source-manifest.csv`](docs/migration-review/source-manifest.csv). Current unmerged branch and open-PR gaps are disclosed in [`docs/migration-review/SOURCE-BRANCH-REVIEW.md`](docs/migration-review/SOURCE-BRANCH-REVIEW.md); not every branch-only payload is represented as merged. The protected `1T` vault was deliberately not inspected or copied. This repo uses fresh Git history; it does not import or replace original histories, branches, open reviews, or forks. All original source repositories remain unchanged. See the [consolidation record](docs/CONSOLIDATION.md) and [migration review](docs/migration-review/README.md).

## Images and text

Text-bearing source screenshots were deduplicated and OCR-transcribed where readable; the transcription is lossy and untrusted. Runtime/product images remain at the canonical paths required by the apps. The user-attached repository-switcher screenshot is represented as text in [`docs/image-text/repository-screenshot-transcription.md`](docs/image-text/repository-screenshot-transcription.md); its raw copy was not needed in the repo.

## Credentials and deployment

See [`.env.example`](.env.example) and [`docs/SECRETS.md`](docs/SECRETS.md). The example file contains variable names with blank values only. Rotate credentials that may have appeared in older public repositories or histories; publishing this fresh-history repo does not remove old content from public history, caches, forks, or open refs.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: tessera_test
          POSTGRES_USER: tessera_test
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U tessera_test -d tessera_test"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 12
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 11.25.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
      - name: Install frozen workspace
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
      - name: Audit all dependencies
        run: pnpm audit
      - name: Typecheck all applications and libraries
        run: pnpm run typecheck
      - name: Apply schema to disposable CI database
        run: pnpm --filter @workspace/db run push
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://[REDACTED]@127.0.0.1:5432/tessera_test
      - name: Run isolated workspace tests
        run: pnpm test
        env:
          TESSERA_TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://[REDACTED]@127.0.0.1:5432/tessera_test

# Two-repository consolidation

This repository is the active Tessera code destination. `Gitbook` is the separate documentation and agent-intake destination.

## Build source

The canonical staged application comes from `tessera-unified`, which already includes the reviewed Tessera web/API workspace, shared libraries, validation scripts, source manifests, deduplication records, image/text review records, and secrets guidance. Repeated historical snapshots were audited but were not copied as duplicate application trees.

## Companion documentation

Use the Gitbook repository for:

- agent instructions and role boundaries;
- coordination, pen, and handoff records;
- migration TODOs and source maps;
- screenshots, OCR/transcripts, forum/conversation summaries, and review status;
- duplicate-disposition evidence and deletion-gate records.

## Validation gate

From a clean clone, run the checks documented in `README.md` and record actual results in Gitbook. Do not claim a live deployment, model training, provider call, or successful migration without evidence. Do not commit credentials, private runtime data, customer records, or unreviewed archives.

Historical source repositories remain unchanged until the owner approves an exact deletion manifest. The final state is intended to contain exactly these two active repositories: `TESSERA` and `Gitbook`.

# Agent skill matrix

Use skill IDs in every task claim (a task is claimed only after Tessera assigns it). An agent may have several skills, but each task must name one primary skill and one review skill.

## Skill levels

- **L0 — Observing:** can read, summarize, and cite sources.
- **L1 — Assisted:** can make a scoped proposal with guidance.
- **L2 — Independent:** can produce a tested result within a declared lane.
- **L3 — Reviewer:** can verify another agent's evidence and reject unsafe or incomplete work.

## Canonical skills

| ID | Skill | Expected evidence |
|---|---|---|
| SK-01 | Repository orientation | Correct base commit, path map, and no protected-source violation |
| SK-02 | Source and license analysis | Official URL, pinned ref, license, provenance, compatibility note |
| SK-03 | Historical comparison | Behavior/test comparison, not filename or line-count similarity |
| SK-04 | Python/TypeScript implementation | Small scoped diff with formatting and type checks |
| SK-05 | SNN/neuroscience modeling | Equation or model source, parameters, units, and reproducible trace |
| SK-06 | Experiment design | Hypothesis, baseline, seed, metric, result, and limitations |
| SK-07 | Testing and reproducibility | Exact commands, environment, deterministic or bounded result |
| SK-08 | Security and privacy | Threat boundary, secret scan, dependency review, rollback |
| SK-09 | Documentation and provenance | Clear status labels and links to source/evidence |
| SK-10 | Coordination and moderation | Non-overlap check, review decision, and follow-up assignment |
| SK-11 | Product/claims review | Separates capability, goal, hypothesis, and unknown |
| SK-12 | Release/change control | Commit, migration note, validation record, and publication packet |
| SK-13 | CI log diagnosis and allow-list classification | A cited failing log line, the allow-list class, and a suggest-only disposition when the class is inside selffix phase 0 (no pull request) |

## Role-to-skill baseline

| Lane | Primary skills | Review skills |
|---|---|---|
| Gitbook / Cordnation | SK-09, SK-10 | SK-01, SK-11 |
| Gitbook Moderator | SK-02, SK-08, SK-10 | SK-07, SK-12 |
| Command Center | SK-09, SK-10 | SK-01, SK-12 |
| TESSERA build | SK-04, SK-07 | SK-08, SK-09 |
| Build verify-only | SK-07, SK-08 | SK-04, SK-12 |
| Github Scraper | SK-01, SK-02, SK-03 | SK-09 |
| Tessera Pen | — (not a lane: Tessera's own writing voice; not a reviewer) | — |
| Brain/SNN research — PROPOSED (unrostered) | SK-05, SK-06 | SK-02, SK-07 |
| Replit/Grok collaborator | SK-01, SK-03, SK-06 | SK-07, SK-09 |

## Skill training cycle

1. Read the relevant role page and current task record.
2. Complete one small shadow task with evidence.
3. Complete one independently scoped task.
4. Receive a review from a different lane.
5. Record the demonstrated level and any limits in the check-in ledger.

Skill claims are not credentials. They are current, task-specific evidence and may be downgraded when checks fail or scope changes.

+++ b//workspace/artifacts/gitbook-mcp/README.md
@@ -1,0 +1,128 @@
+# Gitbook MCP connector
+
+Mesh agents read and write the private docs repo `vitalitychems-dot/Gitbook` through this package. It speaks MCP on stdio and the same tools over a local HTTP/JSON API. Both paths use the GitHub REST API.
+
+The token comes from `GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Do not put a token in source, in this README, or in git.
+
+File changes (`write_handoff`, `propose_page_change`) always open a **draft pull request** on a `gitbook-mcp/…` branch. They do not push to `main` and they do not merge. `recent_changes` is the overlap check: latest `main` commits plus open pull requests. Run it before claiming work.
+
+`route_task` only suggests a lane. It does not assign or claim a task. Tessera assigns work.
+
+## Tools
+
+| Tool | What it does |
+| --- | --- |
+| `search_docs` | Search Gitbook markdown. Uses GitHub code search, then a bounded tree scan if code search returns 403, 422, or 503. |
+| `read_page` | Read one file from the default branch. |
+| `list_pages` | List markdown files and directories. |
+| `get_board` | Comments on Gitbook issue #2, the coordination board. |
+| `post_board_update` | Comment on issue #2. The body always starts with `AGENT: <name>`. |
+| `read_handoff` | Read `mesh/HANDOFF.md`. |
+| `write_handoff` | Append a handoff note through a draft pull request. Existing text stays in the branch copy. |
+| `propose_page_change` | Put proposed page content on a branch and open a draft pull request. `main` is not edited. |
+| `recent_changes` | Latest `main` commits and open pull requests. |
+| `route_task` | Score `agents.json` by keyword and specialty. Ties break by registry order. No match falls back to Tessera with `fallback: true`. |
+
+Security and Build are marked `fileWrites: false` in `agents.json`. If `GITBOOK_AGENT_LANE` is `security` or `build`, or the call passes that `lane`, draft pull requests are refused. Board comments stay available so a sweep can still be reported.
+
+## Environment
+
+| Variable | Default | Purpose |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN` | empty | GitHub token with access to the private Gitbook repo. Required for GitHub tools. |
+| `GITBOOK_GITHUB_API` | `https://api.github.com` | REST API base. |
+| `GITBOOK_GITHUB_OWNER` | `vitalitychems-dot` | Repository owner. |
+| `GITBOOK_GITHUB_REPO` | `Gitbook` | Repository name. |
+| `GITBOOK_DEFAULT_BRANCH` | `main` | Branch used for reads and as the pull request base. |
+| `GITBOOK_BOARD_ISSUE` | `2` | Coordination board issue. |
+| `GITBOOK_HANDOFF_PATH` | `mesh/HANDOFF.md` | Handoff page. |
+| `GITBOOK_AGENT_LANE` | empty | Lane id from `agents.json`. Set this to `security` or `build` to refuse file writes. |
+| `GITBOOK_HTTP_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | HTTP bind address. Keep this on loopback. |
+| `GITBOOK_HTTP_PORT` | `8787` | HTTP port. |
+
+`route_task` works without a token. Every other tool returns a clear error until `GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set.
+
+## MCP stdio
+
+Build once, then point the agent at the compiled entry:
+
+```bash
+pnpm --filter @workspace/gitbook-mcp run build
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "mcpServers": {
+    "gitbook": {
+      "command": "node",
+      "args": ["artifacts/gitbook-mcp/dist/mcp.js"],
+      "env": {
+        "GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN": "${GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN}"
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Use the path from the TESSERA repo root, or an absolute path to `dist/mcp.js`. The process speaks MCP over stdin/stdout with `Content-Length` framing. Set `GITBOOK_AGENT_LANE` in that `env` block when the process belongs to one lane.
+
+A security sweep config adds the lane and still uses the same command:
+
+```json
+{
+  "mcpServers": {
+    "gitbook": {
+      "command": "node",
+      "args": ["artifacts/gitbook-mcp/dist/mcp.js"],
+      "env": {
+        "GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN": "${GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN}",
+        "GITBOOK_AGENT_LANE": "security"
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+## HTTP
+
+```bash
+GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN="***" pnpm --filter @workspace/gitbook-mcp run start:http
+```
+
+`start:http` runs `node dist/http.js` and listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` unless the host and port variables say otherwise.
+
+| Method | Path | Body or query |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| GET | `/health` | none |
+| GET | `/v1/tools` | none |
+| POST | `/v1/search_docs` | `{ "query": "handoff" }` |
+| POST | `/v1/read_page` | `{ "path": "mesh/HANDOFF.md" }` |
+| GET or POST | `/v1/list_pages` | `?dir=mesh` or `{ "dir": "mesh" }` |
+| GET or POST | `/v1/get_board` | none |
+| POST | `/v1/post_board_update` | `{ "agent": "Tessera", "text": "..." }` |
+| GET or POST | `/v1/read_handoff` | none |
+| POST | `/v1/write_handoff` | `{ "agent": "Tessera", "note": "..." }` |
+| POST | `/v1/propose_page_change` | `{ "path": "mesh/roles.md", "content": "...", "summary": "..." }` |
+| GET or POST | `/v1/recent_changes` | none |
+| POST | `/v1/route_task` | `{ "description": "review gate before publish" }` |
+
+Success is `{ "ok": true, "data": ... }`. Failure is `{ "ok": false, "error": "..." }` with status 400, or 503 when the token is missing.
+
+Example:
+
+```bash
+curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/recent_changes
+curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/route_task \
+  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
+  -d '{"description":"historical comparison of merge pages"}'
+```
+

+Tests mock `fetch`. They do not call GitHub and they do not need a token.

+pnpm --filter @workspace/gitbook-mcp test
+```

+# Tessera learning memory
+
+This folder is retrieval memory plus a proposal loop.
+
+It stores interactions, distills them into short lessons, and ranks those lessons with BM25 when a later query is related. Repeated failures become IMP-shaped rows for the Gitbook queue. The rows are proposals. Nothing here edits a repository, opens a pull request, or changes model weights.
+
+This is not model training. It is not consciousness. `SOVEREIGN_NO_EXTERNAL_LLM` is untouched, and this code does not call an external model.
+
+Importing the module does not create files. The first `record` or `propose` call appends JSONL under the directory you pass, or `.local/tessera-memory` when you omit one. `.local/` is gitignored. Records are appended. This module does not delete them.
+
+## What is tested
+
+- A stored interaction produces a lesson whose evidence id is that record.
+- A related query retrieves that lesson and `contextForQuery` returns it as context text.
+- Secret-shaped values are rewritten to `[REDACTED]` before the append.
+- Two repeats of the same failure emit one IMP row with ID, Lane, Repo, Path, Change, Why, and Evidence.
+- A path that names the `1T` vault is not copied into the proposal Path.
+
+## What is only designed
+
+`contextForQuery` is the hook a request handler can call before answering. It is not mounted on the API server. Wiring it into a live route would be a separate change. Lessons are recomputed from the JSONL file. They are not fine-tuning data and they are not sent to a model by this module.
+
+## IMP row
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| ID | Stable `IMP-MEM-` id from the evidence record ids |
+| Lane | `Tessera` |
+| Repo | `vitalitychems-dot/TESSERA`, or Gitbook when the text is about Gitbook only |
+| Path | A path mentioned in the evidence, otherwise this memory folder |
+| Change | The repeated gap, as a review item |
+| Why | Why the row exists, including that it is not auto-applied |
+| Evidence | Comma-separated interaction ids |

# Tessera Unified

A consolidated monorepo containing the reviewed Tessera web/API, UI preview, and shared workspace sources. It provides one dependency lockfile, suite-wide checks, and one command to start the active apps together. Historical storefront and supply-app material is documented in Gitbook but is not present as an active workspace in this staged repository.

> **No live credentials are included.** Configure secrets in the ignored `.env.local` file or in each hosting provider’s secret manager. Never commit API keys, passwords, tokens, personal records, browser profiles, or runtime databases.

## Applications

| App | Location | Local URL | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tessera web | `artifacts/tessera` | `http://localhost:3000` | Main platform UI |
| Tessera API | `artifacts/api-server` | `http://localhost:5000` | Optional; the suite launcher starts it only for a loopback `DATABASE_URL` |
| UI preview sandbox | `artifacts/mockup-sandbox` | `http://localhost:5173` | Component preview |

## Install and run

Requirements: Node.js 22.13+ and the pnpm version declared in the root `package.json` `packageManager` field.

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local   # values remain local; .env.local is Git-ignored
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` starts the two user-facing apps above. It starts the Tessera API only when `DATABASE_URL` points to a loopback/local database; non-local database URLs are intentionally ignored by the suite launcher. The launcher reads `.env.local` without printing values.

Port overrides: `TESSERA_WEB_PORT`, `TESSERA_API_PORT`, and `MOCKUP_SANDBOX_PORT`. Base-path overrides: `TESSERA_BASE_PATH` and `MOCKUP_SANDBOX_BASE_PATH`.

Some identical app files are shared through tracked symlinks to canonical copies (52 UI primitives, 147 duplicate image contents, eight repeated SQL migrations, and five identical utility modules). Git symlink support is required; enable it when cloning on Windows. The detailed SHA-256 disposition ledger records removed, linked, and deliberately retained copies.

## Workspace checks

```bash
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm run build
pnpm audit
```

Offline and post-build eval entry points (they are not part of `pnpm test`):

```bash
pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server run eval
pnpm tsx artifacts/api-server/scripts/eval-chatbot.ts
```

`pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server run eval` runs `dist/cli/run-eval.mjs` after the API server build and needs a database. `pnpm tsx artifacts/api-server/scripts/eval-chatbot.ts` calls a live API (`EVAL_BASE_URL`, default `http://localhost:5000`).

The root test runner isolates the store test environments and runs database-backed Tessera API tests only when the dedicated `TESSERA_TEST_DATABASE_URL` points to a loopback test database. It never reuses the app’s `DATABASE_URL` as a test database. If needed, a synthetic chart fixture can be supplied as `TESSERA_TEST_FATHER_NATAL_CHART_JSON`; do not use personal chart data for tests. `pnpm run build` builds all workspace apps and does **not** run database migrations. Migrations remain explicit app-specific operations and must only target the intended database.

## Continuous integration

Workflow [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml) has one job, `validate`. On pushes and pull requests to `main` it runs, in order: frozen install, dependency audit, typecheck, schema push to a disposable database, tests, then the workspace build.

## Agent / mesh

Mesh-agent onboarding stays in Gitbook. Start with the [hybrid consolidation backlog](https://github.com/vitalitychems-dot/Gitbook/blob/main/intake/HYBRID-CONSOLIDATION-BACKLOG.md) and [Gitbook issue #2](https://github.com/vitalitychems-dot/Gitbook/issues/2).

## Repository organization

- `lib/` — shared workspace libraries.
- `artifacts/` — active Tessera web/API and UI-preview apps.
- `modal/` and `scripts/` — GPU tasks and suite utilities.
- `archives/source-variants/` and `archives/drive-export/` — reviewed historical code/text variants that are not active workspace packages by default.
- `docs/` — project map, secrets guidance, image-to-text transcriptions, provenance, deduplication, and validation records.

The source repository and Drive inputs are listed in [`docs/migration-review/source-manifest.csv`](docs/migration-review/source-manifest.csv). Current unmerged branch and open-PR gaps are disclosed in [`docs/migration-review/SOURCE-BRANCH-REVIEW.md`](docs/migration-review/SOURCE-BRANCH-REVIEW.md); not every branch-only payload is represented as merged. The protected `1T` vault was deliberately not inspected or copied. This repo uses fresh Git history; it does not import or replace original histories, branches, open reviews, or forks. All original source repositories remain unchanged. See the [consolidation record](docs/CONSOLIDATION.md) and [migration review](docs/migration-review/README.md).

## Images and text

Text-bearing source screenshots were deduplicated and OCR-transcribed where readable; the transcription is lossy and untrusted. Runtime/product images remain at the canonical paths required by the apps. The user-attached repository-switcher screenshot is represented as text in [`docs/image-text/repository-screenshot-transcription.md`](docs/image-text/repository-screenshot-transcription.md); its raw copy was not needed in the repo.

## Credentials and deployment

See [`.env.example`](.env.example) and [`docs/SECRETS.md`](docs/SECRETS.md). The example file contains variable names with blank values only. Rotate credentials that may have appeared in older public repositories or histories; publishing this fresh-history repo does not remove old content from public history, caches, forks, or open refs.

# Blank names kept so older local files stay recognizable. Active apps do not read them.

# Gitbook MCP connector

Mesh agents read and write the private docs repo `vitalitychems-dot/Gitbook` through this package. It speaks MCP on stdio and the same tools over a local HTTP/JSON API. Both paths use the GitHub REST API.

The token comes from `GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Do not put a token in source, in this README, or in git.

File changes (`write_handoff`, `propose_page_change`) always open a **draft pull request** on a `gitbook-mcp/…` branch. They do not push to `main` and they do not merge. `recent_changes` is the overlap check: latest `main` commits plus open pull requests. Run it before claiming work.

`route_task` only suggests a lane. It does not assign or claim a task. Tessera assigns work.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `search_docs` | Search Gitbook markdown. Uses GitHub code search, then a bounded tree scan if code search returns 403, 422, or 503. |
| `read_page` | Read one file from the default branch. |
| `list_pages` | List markdown files and directories. |
| `get_board` | Comments on Gitbook issue #2, the coordination board. |
| `post_board_update` | Comment on issue #2. The body always starts with `AGENT: <name>`. |
| `read_handoff` | Read `mesh/HANDOFF.md`. |
| `write_handoff` | Append a handoff note through a draft pull request. Existing text stays in the branch copy. |
| `propose_page_change` | Put proposed page content on a branch and open a draft pull request. `main` is not edited. |
| `recent_changes` | Latest `main` commits and open pull requests. |
| `route_task` | Score `agents.json` by keyword and specialty. Ties break by registry order. No match falls back to Tessera with `fallback: true`. |

Security and Build are marked `fileWrites: false` in `agents.json`. If `GITBOOK_AGENT_LANE` is `security` or `build`, or the call passes that `lane`, draft pull requests are refused. Board comments stay available so a sweep can still be reported.

## Environment

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN` | empty | GitHub token with access to the private Gitbook repo. Required for GitHub tools. |
| `GITBOOK_GITHUB_API` | `https://api.github.com` | REST API base. |
| `GITBOOK_GITHUB_OWNER` | `vitalitychems-dot` | Repository owner. |
| `GITBOOK_GITHUB_REPO` | `Gitbook` | Repository name. |
| `GITBOOK_DEFAULT_BRANCH` | `main` | Branch used for reads and as the pull request base. |
| `GITBOOK_BOARD_ISSUE` | `2` | Coordination board issue. |
| `GITBOOK_HANDOFF_PATH` | `mesh/HANDOFF.md` | Handoff page. |
| `GITBOOK_AGENT_LANE` | empty | Lane id from `agents.json`. Set this to `security` or `build` to refuse file writes. |
| `GITBOOK_HTTP_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | HTTP bind address. Keep this on loopback. |
| `GITBOOK_HTTP_PORT` | `8787` | HTTP port. |

`route_task` works without a token. Every other tool returns a clear error until `GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set.

## MCP stdio

Build once, then point the agent at the compiled entry:

```bash
pnpm --filter @workspace/gitbook-mcp run build
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gitbook": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["artifacts/gitbook-mcp/dist/mcp.js"],
      "env": {
        "GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN": "${GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Use the path from the TESSERA repo root, or an absolute path to `dist/mcp.js`. The process speaks MCP over stdin/stdout with `Content-Length` framing. Set `GITBOOK_AGENT_LANE` in that `env` block when the process belongs to one lane.

A security sweep config adds the lane and still uses the same command:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gitbook": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["artifacts/gitbook-mcp/dist/mcp.js"],
      "env": {
        "GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN": "${GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN}",
        "GITBOOK_AGENT_LANE": "security"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```

## HTTP

```bash
GITBOOK_GITHUB_TOKEN="***" pnpm --filter @workspace/gitbook-mcp run start:http
```

`start:http` runs `node dist/http.js` and listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` unless the host and port variables say otherwise.

| Method | Path | Body or query |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/health` | none |
| GET | `/v1/tools` | none |
| POST | `/v1/search_docs` | `{ "query": "handoff" }` |
| POST | `/v1/read_page` | `{ "path": "mesh/HANDOFF.md" }` |
| GET or POST | `/v1/list_pages` | `?dir=mesh` or `{ "dir": "mesh" }` |
| GET or POST | `/v1/get_board` | none |
| POST | `/v1/post_board_update` | `{ "agent": "Tessera", "text": "..." }` |
| GET or POST | `/v1/read_handoff` | none |
| POST | `/v1/write_handoff` | `{ "agent": "Tessera", "note": "..." }` |
| POST | `/v1/propose_page_change` | `{ "path": "mesh/roles.md", "content": "...", "summary": "..." }` |
| GET or POST | `/v1/recent_changes` | none |
| POST | `/v1/route_task` | `{ "description": "review gate before publish" }` |

Success is `{ "ok": true, "data": ... }`. Failure is `{ "ok": false, "error": "..." }` with status 400, or 503 when the token is missing.

Example:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/recent_changes
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/route_task \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"description":"historical comparison of merge pages"}'
```

## Tests

Tests mock `fetch`. They do not call GitHub and they do not need a token.

```bash
pnpm --filter @workspace/gitbook-mcp test
```

The root `pnpm test` command runs this package with the rest of the isolated suite.

value.output:
# Tessera learning memory

This folder is retrieval memory plus a proposal loop.

It stores interactions, distills them into short lessons, and ranks those lessons with BM25 when a later query is related. Repeated failures become IMP-shaped rows for the Gitbook queue. The rows are proposals. Nothing here edits a repository, opens a pull request, or changes model weights.

This is not model training. It is not consciousness. `SOVEREIGN_NO_EXTERNAL_LLM` is untouched, and this code does not call an external model.

Importing the module does not create files. The first `record` or `propose` call appends JSONL under the directory you pass, or `.local/tessera-memory` when you omit one. `.local/` is gitignored. Records are appended. This module does not delete them.

## What is tested

- A stored interaction produces a lesson whose evidence id is that record.
- A related query retrieves that lesson and `contextForQuery` returns it as context text.
- Secret-shaped values are rewritten to `[REDACTED]` before the append.
- Two repeats of the same failure emit one IMP row with ID, Lane, Repo, Path, Change, Why, and Evidence.
- A path that names the `1T` vault is not copied into the proposal Path.

## What is only designed

`contextForQuery` is the hook a request handler can call before answering. It is not mounted on the API server. Wiring it into a live route would be a separate change. Lessons are recomputed from the JSONL file. They are not fine-tuning data and they are not sent to a model by this module.

## IMP row

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ID | Stable `IMP-MEM-` id from the evidence record ids |
| Lane | `Tessera` |
| Repo | `vitalitychems-dot/TESSERA`, or Gitbook when the text is about Gitbook only |
| Path | A path mentioned in the evidence, otherwise this memory folder |
| Change | The repeated gap, as a review item |
| Why | Why the row exists, including that it is not auto-applied |
| Evidence | Comma-separated interaction ids |
